 Death certificate of Patrick Stewart lists dementia with Lewy bodies, TMZ reports; family asks for Alzheimer’s donations
 Patrick Stewart’s death certificate lists cardiopulmonary arrest and a neurocognitive disorder with Lewy bodies, and Alzheimer’s disease according to TMZ, which obtained it from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. The actor died October 28 at 86, and his family has described a “brief and poignant journey” with the diseases
 By Platform | 2026-11-20 | 1 min read Share f 𝕏 in t w ✈ L @ Official records have confirmed that acclaimed British actor Sir Patrick Stewart died from Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia. According to a death certificate obtained by TMZ, the beloved screen veteran—renowned worldwide for portraying Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men film series—passed away on October 28 at the age of 86.
 The medical documentation further notes cardiopulmonary arrest alongside a neurocognitive disorder involving Lewy bodies, a progressive condition known to impair memory, cognition, and physical movement.
 Read more about this topic:  Sir Patrick Stewart dies at 86 after a landmark seven-decade acting career (with videos) 
 These official findings align with a previous statement from Stewart’s family announcing his passing, which shared that he had experienced “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.”
 Over a celebrated career spanning decades on both stage and screen, Stewart earned widespread admiration from audiences and fellow performers alike for his commanding presence and versatility across theater, television, and blockbuster cinema.
